name: Connecticut
summary: Connecticut is one of the strongest BTM C&I storage markets in ISO-NE. On Apr 1, 2026, the PURA Energy Storage Solutions (ESS) program moved to 'Construct 5': new C&I sites get no upfront rebate, and instead earn 10-year performance payments of $325/kW-yr (small/medium, years 1-5) or $275/kW-yr (large, over 500 kW), dropping to $175/kW-yr in years 6-10. Payment is based on the average kW actually delivered in 30-60 summer and 1-10 winter EDC-called events of up to 3 hours between noon and 9pm. Eversource demand charges are high and billed on monthly maximum demand (Rate 30 about $27/kW-mo distribution plus transmission; Rate 35 about $25.5/kW-mo), so peak shaving and ESS stack well when SOC is managed on event days. ISO-NE capacity tags are worth roughly $31-43/kW-yr (FCA 17/18, unscaled), but only reach customers on pass-through supply contracts. Key risks: the pending CL&P rate case (rates about July 2027), unverified large-TOU and UI demand values, the export/non-export eligibility question under ESS, the NFPA 855 600 kWh indoor fire-area cap, and the stalled 2026 CT fire code.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: ICAP tag = customer load at the ISO-NE annual system peak hour in the prior Jun-May year; recalculated each spring and effective Jun 1-May 31
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: Proxy = FCA 18 clearing price $3.580/kW-month x 12 = $42.96/kW-yr (2027/28). A peak cut in summer 2027 sets the 2028/29 tag, whose price is not yet known, so FCA 18 is used as the proxy. 2026/27 (FCA 17): $2.590 x 12 = $31.08/kW-yr. The ISO-NE capacity-requirement scaling and loss gross-up, which typically raise the $/kW-tag value, are not applied because they were not verified.
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: Realized only if the competitive supply contract passes capacity through (index or pass-through) or at contract renewal. Standard Service and LRS customers capture it only indirectly through class-average pricing.

tariffs.storage_notes: Distribution plus transmission demand totals about $27.06/kW-month before riders, all hours, every month, so monthly NCP shaving is the main bill value. Rate eligibility is set by maximum demand, so shaving can affect rate-class migration. Check the tariff's migration rules.

programs.name: Energy Storage Solutions (ESS) - C&I Active Dispatch, 'Construct 5' (new enrollments from Apr 1, 2026)
programs.administrator: CT Green Bank, Eversource and UI (overseen by PURA; annual review in the XX-08-05 dockets; the 2026 restructure came from the Docket 25-08-05 review)
programs.status_notes: Since Apr 1, 2026, all new participants enroll in Construct 5. It replaces the upfront $/kWh incentive and Passive Dispatch with a small enrollment incentive plus 10-year performance payments for Active Dispatch only. A $350 non-refundable application fee applies to all new C&I applications. Program-wide, more than 140 MW of C&I was approved before the restructure. The original goal was 580 MW, with a 1 GW by 2030 storage goal cited. The remaining 2026 capacity or budget was not verified.

eligibility.other: Customer of Eversource or UI. The class (small/medium/large) is set by annual peak demand. The kW eligible for incentive is capped at 150% of annual peak demand or 2 MW, 'whichever is greater' per the summary; verify, as this may be 'lesser'. Priority customers are critical facilities, grid-edge, small businesses, and C&I sites replacing onsite fossil generation. Only batteries with an interconnection agreement may export. A 2025 review allowed existing non-export batteries interconnected before 2026 to enroll. Whether NEW non-export C&I systems qualify under Construct 5 is unverified.

valuation.kw_basis: Average kW-AC delivered across all Active Dispatch events in the season, measured from inverter data, not nameplate. Settled at the end of each summer and winter season.
valuation.cap: Eligible kW is capped at 150% of annual peak demand or 2 MW (see eligibility note)

tiers.label: Priority C&I enrollment incentive (one-time)
tiers.conditions: $/kWh per ESS program-changes page. One secondary source says $/kW, so verify the unit. Non-priority C&I gets no enrollment incentive.

valuation.notes: Annual payment = rate x average kW delivered during events. Whether the $/kW-yr is split between summer and winter seasons, and how, was not verified. Under-delivery directly reduces payment. A 3-hour event at full kW needs usable kWh of at least 3 x kW, so deliverable kW = min(inverter kW, usable kWh / 3).

dispatch.window: Events up to 3 h within 12pm-9pm (summer). Event length is 1-3 h.
dispatch.notice: Called by the EDC (Eversource or UI) on high-demand days. Notice lead time not verified.
dispatch.baseline_or_mv: Inverter or battery telemetry (kW-AC output during events), not a meter baseline

stacking.notes: Demand-charge shaving on non-event days stacks freely. On event days the battery must hold SOC for the 12-9pm window. Summer events are likely to overlap the ISO-NE annual peak hour, which helps the ICAP tag. Dual participation in ISO-NE wholesale markets (ADCR or FCM via an aggregator) is NOT verified, so check the Terms and Conditions.

programs.vpp_relevance: The EDCs already dispatch the batteries centrally, so a developer VPP should treat ESS events as the priority dispatch signal and layer bill optimization around them. Fleet telemetry from the inverters forms the M&V basis.

panel_notes.topic: Construct 5 pays on delivered kW, not nameplate
panel_notes.note: Under Construct 5 the whole incentive is the average kW-AC delivered across every event. A 200 kW/418 kWh unit sustains only about 139 kW for 3 hours, so model deliverable kW = min(kW, usable kWh / 3) after SOC reserves and losses. Missed or partial events cut the 10-year payment directly.

panel_notes.topic: Rate case risk on demand charges
panel_notes.note: CL&P filed its first full rate case since 2017 in May 2026, seeking about 11%, with new rates expected around July 2027. Distribution demand rates and design (kW vs kVA, TOU windows) could change. Do not escalate today's $/kW flat for 10 years, and run a sensitivity.

Eversource rate classes break at 200, 350 and 1,000 kW of maximum demand. Shaving can move a site across a threshold, which changes both the $/kW and the billing basis (NCP kW vs on-peak kVA). Model the bill on the post-battery rate class.

panel_notes.topic: UI demand floors and missing data
panel_notes.note: UI GST carries a $/kW minimum charge ($8.71 summer, $7.41 winter) on Peak Demand, which can limit distribution-demand savings. LPT demand rates were not retrieved. Get the current UI rate schedule before quoting savings in New Haven or Bridgeport.
UI calls ESS events for batteries in its own territory, separately from Eversource. A cross-territory VPP gets two dispatch signals and two settlement calendars.

CT ICAP tag savings (about $31-43/kW-yr at FCA 17/18 prices, unscaled) reach the customer only on index or pass-through capacity contracts, or at renewal. Most fixed all-in C&I contracts keep the savings with the supplier. Contract structure matters as much as battery dispatch.

ESS-enrolled batteries are dispatched by the EDC. Before layering ISO-NE ADCR, FCM, or reserve participation, confirm the ESS T&Cs on dual participation, telemetry, and whose dispatch takes priority. ISO-NE's move to a prompt capacity auction for 2028+ changes forward capacity revenue assumptions.

On a non-export interconnection the battery can only offset coincident site load. A retail site with a 120 kW evening load and a 200 kW battery earns ESS on at most about 120 kW. Check 12-9pm interval load on event-type days, or pursue an export or flexible-interconnection agreement.

panel_notes.topic: Indoor fire-area limit and code edition
panel_notes.note: NFPA 855 caps indoor Li-ion at 600 kWh per fire area (absent large-scale fire testing or AHJ approval). The 2026 CT fire code (NFPA 1-2024) is stalled at the LRRC, so marshals may apply 2022 CSFPC provisions. Plan outdoor UL 9540 cabinets with setbacks, and confirm the edition with the local fire marshal early.

panel_notes.topic: kVA billing on large TOU rates
panel_notes.note: Eversource Rates 57 and 58 bill demand per kVA. A 4-quadrant PCS can provide VARs to cut kVA, but enabling this needs EDC approval of the inverter settings. Model the kVA demand with the site's power factor, not kW alone.

Under 500 kW gets the new expedited commercial track; up to 2 MW goes Fast Track. Stacking 200 kW units past 500 kW can push a project into longer screening. Consider PCS export limiting so the screened capacity stays under the thresholds.
